revealWordProblem.title: Apply: Build the Arcade Scoreboard
revealWordProblem.text: You are programming the scoreboard for a new arcade game. A player clears 7/8 of the level. The leaderboard must show this score as a percent, and the game engine stores it as a decimal. What percent and what decimal should the scoreboard display for 7/8? Show how you converted between all three forms.
revealWordProblem.sampleAnswer: 7 ÷ 8 = 0.875, and 0.875 × 100 = 87.5%. So 7/8 = 0.875 = 87.5%. The leaderboard shows 87.5% and the game engine stores 0.875.

conceptIntro.heading: Let's build it together — How can one value be written as a fraction, a decimal, AND a percent?
conceptIntro.intro: Equivalent forms name the same value in different ways. A fraction, a decimal, and a percent can all show the same amount. We'll walk through a worked example, try one together, then you'll try a few with hints right there when you need them.
conceptIntro.keyIdea: To turn a fraction into a percent, divide the top by the bottom to get a decimal, then multiply by 100.

iDo.title: Watch me
lines: A player scored 3/4 of the points. I want this as a decimal and a percent.
First I divide: 3 ÷ 4 = 0.75. That is the decimal.
So 3/4 = 0.75 = 75%. All three name the same score.

discourse.prompt: What pattern do you notice when converting between fractions, decimals, and percents?
discourse.sentenceFrame: To convert a fraction to a percent, I can ___ because ___.

choiceFeedback: Try again: 3 ÷ 5 × 100.
Divide the numerator by the denominator, then multiply by 100.
Check your calculation.
hints: 3/5 means 3 divided by 5. A percent is just that decimal scaled to 'out of 100'.
Convert fraction → decimal → percent: divide, then multiply the decimal by 100.
Start with 3 ÷ 5 = 0.6. Now move the decimal point two places right to name it as a percent.

choiceFeedback: Double-check: 7 ÷ 20 × 100.
Divide 7 by 20 first, then convert to a percent.
Review your arithmetic.
hints: The denominator 20 is friendly: 20 × 5 = 100, and percents are always 'out of 100'.
Make an equivalent fraction with denominator 100 by multiplying top AND bottom by the same number.
Multiply 7/20 by 5/5: the bottom becomes 100. Whatever the top becomes is your percent.

approaching.explanation: To convert a percent to a decimal, divide by 100: 45 ÷ 100 = 0.45.
choiceFeedback: Divide the percent by 100, or move the decimal point left 2 places.
Check your percent-to-decimal conversion.
Remember: a percent is per 100.
hints: Percent means 'per 100', so 45% is really 45 out of 100.
To turn a percent into a decimal, divide by 100 — the decimal point slides two places to the LEFT.
Start at 45. and move the decimal two places left: 45 → 4.5 → where does it land after the second hop?

approaching.explanation: 0.75 = 75/100. Simplify by dividing both by 25: 75÷25 = 3 and 100÷25 = 4. So 0.75 = 3/4.
choiceFeedback: Think: 0.75 = 75/100. Can you simplify that fraction?
Try converting the decimal to a fraction with 100 in the denominator.
Look for a fraction equivalent to 0.75.
hints: 0.75 is read 'seventy-five hundredths' — the place value tells you the denominator.
Write the decimal as a fraction over 100, then simplify by dividing top and bottom by a common factor.
Write 75/100, then divide both the 75 and the 100 by 25 to simplify.

approaching.title: Spot the Common Mistake

workedExample.label: Read the digits as the percent
workedExample.work: The numerator is 3 and the denominator is 5, so the student writes 35%.

approaching.correctWork: You cannot just read the digits. Divide first: 3 ÷ 5 = 0.6, then multiply by 100. So 3/5 = 0.6 = 60%, not 35%.
hints: Does writing the two digits 3 and 5 actually divide 3 by 5?
Divide 3 ÷ 5 to get 0.6, then × 100 → 60%.

approaching.stem: A game shows your score as 7/8 complete. What percent is that?
choiceFeedback: Divide 7 by 8, then multiply by 100.
Convert the fraction to a decimal first.
Check your calculation on the conversion.
hints: 7/8 means 7 divided by 8 — the answer will be a decimal just under 1, so the percent is just under 100%.
Divide the numerator by the denominator, then multiply the decimal by 100 to get the percent.
Compute 7 ÷ 8 = 0.875. Now slide the decimal two places right to read it as a percent.

onLevel.title: Spot the Common Mistake

workedExample.label: Divide the bottom by the top

onLevel.correctWork: The student divided in the wrong order. To turn a fraction into a decimal, divide the TOP by the bottom: 5 ÷ 8 = 0.625, then × 100 → 62.5%. So 5/8 = 0.625 = 62.5%. (A check: 5/8 is less than 1, so the percent must be under 100%, never 160%.)
hints: Is 5/8 more or less than one whole? Then can its percent be over 100%?
Divide the numerator by the denominator: 5 ÷ 8 = 0.625, so 5/8 = 62.5%.

onLevel.stem: Your arcade scoreboard reads 0.25 of the level cleared. What percent and fraction match this score?
onLevel.explanation: Move the decimal two places: 0.25 = 25%. As a fraction, 0.25 = 25/100 = 1/4.
choiceFeedback: Remember: multiply the decimal by 100, or move the decimal point right 2 places.
Check your conversion — 0.25 as a percent should be higher.
Double-check your decimal-to-percent conversion.

onLevel.stem: A player powered up 3/5 of the energy bar. Which decimal and percent name the same amount?
choiceFeedback: Divide 3 by 5 to get the decimal, then multiply by 100 for the percent.
Check both the decimal and percent conversions.
Try dividing the fraction to get the decimal first.

onLevel.title: Level 2 Extension — Find the Decimal-to-Percent Mistake
onLevel.correctWork: To change a decimal to a percent, multiply by 100 (move the decimal two places RIGHT): 0.4 × 100 = 40. So 0.4 = 40%, not 4%.
hints: Which way does the decimal move when you go from a decimal to a percent — left or right?
Going decimal → percent means multiply by 100, so the point moves two places right: 0.4 becomes 40%, not 4%.

onLevel.title: Find the Conversion Error
hints: 2 ÷ 3 doesn't terminate — is 0.67 the exact decimal?
0.67 is rounded. The precise decimal is 0.666... (repeating), making the percent 66.7% or 66⅔%.

onLevel.prompt: A student says 3/8 is greater than 40% because 3 and 8 are bigger numbers than 4 and 0. Is the student correct? Convert both values to the same form and explain.
onLevel.sentenceFrame: The student is ___ because 3/8 = ___ = ___%, which is ___ than 40%.
onLevel.hint: Convert 3/8 and 40% to the same form (both fractions or both percents) so you can compare them fairly.
hints: Bigger digits do NOT mean a bigger value — 3/8 and 40% can only be compared in the same form.
Turn 3/8 into a percent (divide, then multiply by 100) so both values are percents.
Compute 3 ÷ 8 = 0.375. Multiply by 100 to get its percent, then say whether that percent is above or below 40%.

practice.commonMistake: A common mistake in Relate Fractions, Decimals, and Percents is treating the numerator and denominator as the percent's digits instead of dividing — for example, turning 3/5 into "35%" by just reading the 3 and the 5, instead of dividing 3 ÷ 5 = 0.6 and multiplying by 100 to get the correct 60%. A second version of this mistake is dividing the denominator by the numerator (flipping the division), like computing 8 ÷ 5 = 1.6 for 5/8 instead of 5 ÷ 8 = 0.625 — always divide the top (numerator) by the bottom (denominator), never the other way around.
